rubric.role_summary: Senior product engineer building talent acquisition and HR software, owning substantial product areas and delivering features end-to-end across the stack.
rubric.search_query:
Find candidates for this role:
Senior product engineer building talent acquisition and HR software, owning substantial product areas and delivering features end-to-end across the stack.
Mandatory professional qualifications:
- Has previously led or taken ownership of projects.
Preferred, not mandatory:
- Enjoys working with typed languages.
Work location and geographic eligibility:
Accept any one of these geographic alternatives (OR): United States. Specific cities and metropolitan areas also include any location within about 100 miles (160 km) of them; states, countries, and regions require a location inside them. Remote candidates must currently be located in one of these areas; remote work does not remove this geographic condition.

must_haves.requirement: Has previously led or taken ownership of projects.
must_haves.source_quote: You haven’t led or taken ownership of projects before.

preferences.source_quote: a love of typed languages is helpful

location.requirement_text: Location: United States (remote). This is the role's single location rule: candidates must currently be located in it. Specific cities and metropolitan areas also include any location within about 100 miles (160 km) of them; states, countries, and regions require a location inside them.

soft_requirements: Comfort tackling different parts of a technology stack and handling product and technical ambiguity.
Balances speed and quality, seeks feedback, and looks for ways to improve skills and create leverage.
Collaborates and communicates clearly with stakeholders and other engineers.
Maintains a project-level perspective rather than getting lost in implementation details.

interpretation.user_instruction: for multiple locations, accept either one, broaden the area to the general area if it's a specific city, if remote + a location, please force them into the location, follow the text rather than the metadata, for x-y years exp, unbound the top but evaluate obviously overqualified candidates as failures in the final fit eval, other than that, assume the less strict of interpretations (eg masters required versus masters or phd, eval as if masters or phd)
